canonical_layer_boundary: Silver layer (silver_reconciliation_standard) — confirmed by engineer 2026-07-23, see discovery/INTAKE_SUMMARY.md

nodes.name: Invoice
nodes.business_definition: [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23]: A single line item on a vendor's monthly statement representing one unpaid or disputed charge — a parts order, sublet repair, or towing charge — that VIVE owes or has paid, identified by an invoice number the vendor assigns.
nodes.lifecycle_summary: [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23]: Received on a vendor PDF -> extracted -> normalized into Silver -> compared against internal ERP records -> resolved as matched or surfaced as an exception for AP review.
nodes.extraction_note: One Invoice record exists per (statement, source) pair — the same underlying schema row represents either a vendor-statement-reported invoice or VIVE's internal ERP record of that invoice, distinguished by the record_source attribute (see SV-001). This is why record_source is modeled as an attribute-governing vocabulary rather than a type split into two entities: docs/VIVE_Implementation_Context.md explicitly frames both sides as sharing one schema so a future real-NetSuite integration only has to swap what feeds the INTERNAL_ERP side. Co-owned by two writer modules (M-014 for VENDOR_STATEMENT rows, M-037 for INTERNAL_ERP rows) — confirmed via TOPOLOGY.md A02 call trace, not assumed. synonyms: NOT DETERMINABLE FROM SOURCE — no team-specific alternate naming confirmed yet (engineer, 2026-07-23).

nodes.name: record_id
nodes.business_meaning: System-generated surrogate identifier — SHA-256 hash of (record_source, statement_id, invoice_number, outstanding_amount). Not a business-facing invoice identifier.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: computed via hashlib.sha256(...) before every INSERT in normalize_to_silver()/normalize_erp_to_silver() (notebooks/01_document_intake.py, src/mock_erp/generator.py); also UNIQUE NOT NULL (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql). No code path constructs a Silver row without first computing this value.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Not the natural business key — see A-009 (invoice_number) for that. record_id exists to make Silver rows individually addressable for the Gold-layer join (statement_record_id/erp_record_id).

nodes.name: record_source
nodes.business_meaning: Which side of the reconciliation this row represents — the vendor's own statement, or VIVE's internal ERP record of the same invoice.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: hardcoded literal ('VENDOR_STATEMENT' or 'INTERNAL_ERP') in every INSERT in normalize_to_silver()/normalize_erp_to_silver(); also NOT NULL + CHECK-constrained in schema. Not computed from possibly-missing source data — a constant per code path.

nodes.name: document_type
nodes.business_meaning: Classification of the source document this row was derived from.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: same pattern as A-002 — hardcoded literal ('VENDOR_STATEMENT' / 'MOCK_ERP_EXTRACT') in both normalize functions. Schema allows null; code never produces it.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Values overlap in spelling with record_source's VENDOR_STATEMENT value (see SVV-001/SVV-003) — two distinct vocabularies, easy to conflate.

nodes.name: statement_id
nodes.business_meaning: Identifier for the specific reconciliation run/batch this invoice record belongs to.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: NOT NULL-constrained, and always supplied as a parameter to normalize_to_silver()/normalize_erp_to_silver(), itself always generated in run_intake() (statement_id = f"STMT-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8].upper()}" if not explicitly passed) before any Silver write occurs.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Functions as a 'reconciliation run identity,' not reliably as 'the identity of the original extraction event' — a cache-hit re-run creates a new Silver record under a fresh statement_id while reusing Bronze data still filed under the original statement_id (F02 Naming Pattern Flags). Flagged as an open question, not resolved here.

nodes.name: statement_date
nodes.business_meaning: Intended to be the statement's issuance date.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: always populated from row.get("statement_period") in normalize_to_silver() — since statement_period (A-023) is itself always set, this field is never null as a direct consequence.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Code-confirmed: notebooks/01_document_intake.py's normalize_to_silver() populates this field from statement_period (a YYYY-MM string), not a real extracted date — its own inline comment reads '# statement_date — use period as proxy'. This field currently carries no information beyond A-023 (statement_period).

nodes.name: vendor_id
nodes.business_meaning: Internally-derived vendor grouping key (uppercased, underscored form of the vendor name or filename stem) — not an identifier issued by any external system.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: always derived in run_intake() before Bronze is written (from the filename stem initially, then overwritten from the always-non-null vendor name once extraction completes — see A-007's fallback). Always a non-empty string by construction.

nodes.name: vendor_name
nodes.business_meaning: The vendor/supplier company name.
nodes.null_semantic: [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23]: ABSENT, confirmed isolated to two orphaned test-seed statement_ids (STMT-1291E89D, STMT-A00DDA29) with zero Bronze/intake-log/cache footprint — not a defect in the live intake pipeline's vendor_name fallback. Root cause of the seed data itself is not determinable (no git history to trace which script inserted it).
nodes.disambiguation_note: 40% null in observed data (F02). The 1,299 INTERNAL_ERP-side nulls are by design (normalize_erp_to_silver() hardcodes None — ERP Bronze never stores a vendor name). The remaining ~424 VENDOR_STATEMENT-side nulls are fully accounted for by the two orphaned test-seed statement_ids above — investigated 2026-07-23: neither has any row in bronze_vendor_statement_raw, document_intake_log, or extraction_cache, so they were never produced by run_intake()'s normal pipeline (which guarantees a non-null vendor_name via derive_vendor_name_from_filename() before Bronze is ever written). Not a live-pipeline gap.

nodes.name: shop
nodes.business_meaning: The specific VIVE Collision shop/location the invoice pertains to.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: invoice_number
nodes.business_meaning: The invoice number exactly as printed on the source document — the natural business identifier for an invoice. Stored verbatim, whitespace-trimmed only (RULE-01) — no normalization, since divergent vendor/ERP formatting is a real discrepancy to surface, not paper over.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: guaranteed by get_skip_reason() (notebooks/01_document_intake.py), which skips a row outright before validation if it has neither invoice_number nor ro_number ('no invoice identifier found'), and by validate_invoice()'s required_fields check (config/validation/extraction_rules.json: ["invoice_number", "outstanding_amount"]), which diverts any row still missing invoice_number to the review queue. No row reaches Silver without one.

nodes.name: invoice_number_normalized
nodes.business_meaning: Intended to hold a normalized form of the invoice number for matching purposes.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: always derived via normalize_invoice_number() (src/normalization.py) applied directly to invoice_number, which is itself guaranteed non-null (see A-009). normalize_invoice_number() only returns falsy given a falsy input, which cannot happen here.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Under the current RULE-01 design (whitespace-trim only, no real normalization), this field is currently identical to A-009 (invoice_number) in every observed case — it exists as a placeholder for a future vendor-specific normalization profile, not because it currently differs.

nodes.name: invoice_date
nodes.business_meaning: The date the invoice was issued.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: ro_number
nodes.business_meaning: Repair order number — the vendor/shop's reference for the specific repair job this invoice line pertains to. Used as the Level 2 matching key (RO + amount) when an exact invoice-number match fails.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: po_number
nodes.business_meaning: Purchase order number, where applicable.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: work_order_number
nodes.business_meaning: Work order number, a dealer-specific reference distinct from RO/PO numbers.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: amount
nodes.business_meaning: The original invoice/charge amount.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: write_to_bronze()/normalize_to_silver() compute amount with a fallback chain (amount = safe_float(raw_amount) or safe_float(raw_outstanding_amount)), and validate_invoice()'s pre-processing step (if outstanding_amount is None and amount is not None: outstanding_amount = amount) plus the required_fields check on outstanding_amount together guarantee at least one of amount/outstanding_amount was present before a row reaches Bronze.

nodes.name: credit
nodes.business_meaning: Any credit or payment applied against the invoice.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: outstanding_amount
nodes.business_meaning: The amount still owed — this is the figure the matching engine actually compares (RULE hierarchy operates on outstanding_amount, not amount).
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: outstanding_amount is in validate_invoice()'s required_fields (config/validation/extraction_rules.json) — any row missing it is diverted to the review queue before Bronze/Silver, per the same validation gate as invoice_number (A-009).

nodes.name: due_date
nodes.business_meaning: Payment due date.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: posting_date
nodes.business_meaning: The date this invoice was posted in VIVE's ERP.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE
nodes.disambiguation_note: An ERP-only concept — always null on the VENDOR_STATEMENT side by design (normalize_to_silver() hardcodes None), populated on the INTERNAL_ERP side only when a source invoice_date existed to compute a posting lag from (src/mock_erp/generator.py).

nodes.name: status
nodes.business_meaning: The invoice's posting status in VIVE's ERP.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE
nodes.disambiguation_note: An ERP-only concept — confirmed null on exactly all 3,031 VENDOR_STATEMENT-side rows and non-null on all 1,299 INTERNAL_ERP-side rows (F02), a clean structural split, not partial data loss. Governed by SV-003.

nodes.name: description
nodes.business_meaning: Free-text line-item description.
nodes.null_semantic: ABSENT

nodes.name: currency
nodes.business_meaning: Currency of the amount fields.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE
nodes.disambiguation_note: Currently always 'USD' when populated (hardcoded in every AI provider client's schema builder, not genuinely extracted) and always null on the INTERNAL_ERP side (hardcoded None in normalize_erp_to_silver()) — not a real multi-currency capability today despite the field's presence.

nodes.name: statement_period
nodes.business_meaning: The billing period (YYYY-MM) this statement covers — the actual field A-005 (statement_date) currently just duplicates.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: always defaulted in run_intake() (if not statement_period: statement_period = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m")) before any Bronze/Silver write occurs; never left unset.

nodes.name: source_file
nodes.business_meaning: The originating file — the source PDF's filename for VENDOR_STATEMENT rows, or the literal 'MOCK_ERP' for INTERNAL_ERP rows.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: on the VENDOR_STATEMENT side, always os.path.basename(pdf_path) (write_to_bronze(), requiring a real, validated file path per run_intake()'s own FileNotFoundError guard); on the INTERNAL_ERP side, always the hardcoded literal "MOCK_ERP" (normalize_erp_to_silver()).

nodes.name: ingestion_timestamp
nodes.business_meaning: When this Silver row was written.
nodes.null_semantic: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23, code-derived]: always datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), computed once per function call in both normalize_to_silver() and normalize_erp_to_silver() before the insert loop; never left unset.

nodes.business_meaning: This record reflects what the vendor's own statement reported.

nodes.disambiguation_note: Same literal string also appears as a document_type value (SVV-003) in a different vocabulary — do not conflate.

nodes.disambiguation_note: Same literal string also appears as a record_source value (SVV-001) in a different vocabulary — do not conflate.

nodes.business_meaning: The invoice has been posted in VIVE's ERP.
nodes.transition_trigger: NOT_APPLICABLE — [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23]: terminal, non-transitioning classification (confirmed by engineer) — no outgoing transition exists from this state.

nodes.business_meaning: The invoice exists in the ERP but has not yet posted.
nodes.transition_trigger: [ENGINEER NOTE — 2026-07-23]: Not yet observed because the Mock ERP generator (RULE-06 placeholder) always assigns POSTED by default. PENDING exists in the schema for the eventual real NetSuite integration, where the real-world trigger would be VIVE's AP team or NetSuite marking the transaction posted. This is forward-looking design intent, not an observed behavior.
nodes.disambiguation_note: Code-possible (src/mock_erp/generator.py's pending_posting scenario config option) but never observed in any recorded run across either database (F02) — zero live exercise of this value or its transition to POSTED.
